sonnet.problem: The right answer 'altar' already appeared as a wrong answer on card 4 ('He gathers stones for the altar'). That earlier card gives away this blank, and reuses an answer already shown.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: Stop 1 card 10 already showed the right answer 'God Himself will provide the lamb'. A baker can pick 'The LORD Will Provide' just by matching the word 'provide', so an earlier card gives away this answer.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to complete a line of the promise ('all ___ of the earth will be blessed'). Nothing on a card lets the baker reason out 'nations' over 'kings' or 'cities', so it is a wording guess.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: This summary card for the list of Nahor's sons goes item by item. It names Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah, which are not standout details.
sonnet.rule: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. He can name a standout detail the text gives if it helps the stretch stick.
